- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–2% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to align with downward momentum.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; cap forecast peaks at 1.5x the prior 3-day average to prevent overcorrection.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, model tends to hold or slightly overcorrect; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day of negative trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently misses late-period price corrections; adjust final 5–7 days downward if sentiment turns negative or stabilizes near zero.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for each cycle shift toward bullish sentiment.
